correctness.rationale: Under the finite max product metric, two-sided delta-pseudo-orbit spaces factor coordinatewise, so product of factor continuous selectors is a selector. Ordinary induced shadowing and two-sided limit shadowing pass through a finite maximum. Artigue Prop. 5.3 local self-tuning discrepancy for each factor is bounded by the product discrepancy, so minimum factor thresholds works. Conversely, embed the active factor pseudo-orbit with exact orbit trajectories in every other coordinate; this preserves jump bounds and yields equality of the weighted sequence discrepancy with the active discrepancy, and projection of the product selector induces each relevant shadowing property. On genuine orbits the selector returns the initial point. Nonempty factors, m finite, positive common mu and compact homeomorphisms are essential assumptions. Source Propositions 3.2 and 5.3 were read for the reductions; neither numerical testing nor the ordinary shadowing property alone is used.
